messages:
Support Sarah: heads-up — a dedicated-customer on eu-west reported sudden p95/p99 spikes right after we pushed the driver/CUDA bundle last night. they see API timeouts and backend retries. their SLAs are getting hit. attaching their rough trace: high tail on /v1/complete route.
Maya Chen: thanks — any repro steps from the customer? is this only eu-west or global?
Support Sarah: customer says it started ~2026-03-14T23:40Z (after our 23:30 deploy). only eu-west so far, but they route to dedicated pool eu-west-2. they collected a few spans showing GPU wait + long nvme wait.
Raj Patel: can someone paste the deploy tag? iirc we pushed CUDA 12.4 + nvidia-driver 525.60.13 to the dedicated fleet.
Alex Kim: correct — image tag runtime:v2026.03.14-driver-525.60.13-cuda12.4.
JD (infra): i'm starting an audit on nodes that had the upgrade. running `kubectl get nodes -l pool=dedicated-eu-west -o wide` now. also pulling `dmesg` and `iostat -x 1 5` from affected hosts.
SRE-bot: alert: p99 latency for route /v1/complete exceeded 3s in eu-west-dedicated (3.6s) — spikes at 23:45 UTC.
Maya Chen: check `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` and NVML logs. if GPU driver misbehaving we should see NVML timeouts or ECC errors.
Alex Kim: paste from one host `dmesg | tail -n 30`:
```
[Mar 14 23:43:12] nvidia: probe error, timeout waiting for device
[Mar 14 23:43:13] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[Mar 14 23:43:13] kworker/u32: #2 hung for 123s
```
Raj Patel: that blk_update_request + kworker hang screams storage I/O contention / driver interaction. could be kernel+NVMe firmware + new driver combos. we saw similar when host kernel changed I/O scheduler defaults.
JD (infra): iostat shows %util at 99% with avgqu-sz jumping — small random reads dominating. running `fio --name=randread --iodepth=16 --bs=4k --size=1G --numjobs=2 --runtime=60` reproduces high latency on that host.
Support Sarah: customer provided request shape: many small chat completions (short prompts, 8-32 tokens) at high concurrency. workload favors small random reads from KV cache persisted to local nvme.
Maya Chen: that aligns — when backend hits storage stalls, GPU threads wait for data leading to p99. possible root candidates: 1) driver/CUDA introducing more synchronous page faults 2) NVMe firmware regression 3) kernel change affecting IO paths 4) our KV caching falling back to disk more often.
Alex Kim: quick mitigation options: - roll traffic away from affected dedicated nodes by changing routing policy (route to healthy pool) - temporarily increase in-memory cache TTL so fewer disk reads - throttle per-tenant concurrency (support rule) - rollback driver on a canary host to previous known-good (525.51.x)
Raj Patel: i can test driver rollback on one spare host. steps: `sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-525.51.05 && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` then run `python3 load_test.py --shape small` to mimic customer. will report perf delta.
JD (infra): also opening cloud storage ticket — looks like underlying NVMe controller firmware jumped to 52.23 on the new AMI. i'm rolling one node to old AMI (firmware 51.10) to see if it helps.
SRE-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0819 assigned to eng-runtime oncall.
Maya Chen: good. make sure we gather perf counters: `nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o DT` and `perf top` during repro. also capture `strace -f` on the model-server worker to see syscall stalls (futex? pread?).
Alex Kim: after I rolled driver back on canary node, p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 0.9s on the canary, throughput steady. looks convincing.
Support Sarah: customer confirmed better latency when routed to older nodes. they want ETA on fix.
Raj Patel: root cause hypothesis: 525.60.13 changes GPU memory management causing more page-fault syncs that amplify under storage stalls; combined with NVMe firmware 52.23 introducing long tail read latencies. kernel IO path changes made it worse.
Maya Chen: next steps: 1) roll back driver on all affected dedicated nodes (plan + safety windows) 2) pin AMI/firmware to 51.10 where possible 3) throttle rollout of CUDA/driver bundles until we complete lab repro 4) add short-term routing policy to avoid single-pool dependence 5) add telemetry: NVML timeouts, blk io histograms to console dashboards.
JD (infra): i'm preparing a rolling rollback job to replace nodes with prior AMI/driver combo; will annotate nodes with `taint=driver-regression:NoSchedule` during work. ETA for full fleet rollback ~90 minutes if no surprises.
Support Sarah: i'll update the customer with rollback plan and offer routing to healthy pool in the meantime. also offering 10% credit for SLA breach.
Maya Chen: please also open a vendor bug with Nvidia and the NVMe vendor: include `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1`, and fio samples. tag NV-9982. I'll put repro scripts in the internal repo under `infra/repro/driver-nvme-tail`.
Alex Kim: temporary software mitigations: - increase KV cache memory hold to reduce disk fallback - tune storage I/O scheduler on hosts (`mq-deadline` -> `none`) and set `nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us` if available - enable per-request throttling in router to flatten bursts
Raj Patel: noting one more: add automatic fallback to smaller quantized model variant for affected tenants while we remediate so p99 remains acceptable.
SRE-bot: update: rollback job started at 2026-03-15T01:05Z.
Support Sarah: customer replied: appreciate quick action, will monitor. please keep me posted so I can escalate if anything changes.
Maya Chen: good work team. after rollback completes, we should run a matrix of kernel/driver/firmware combos and publish a compatibility matrix in docs so future deploys are gated. also add a preflight fio test in the AMI bake pipeline.
JD (infra): agreed — filing infra-ticket INFRA-2026-432 to add fio preflight + NVML checks to AMI CI.
Alex Kim: will follow up with postmortem including timelines, root cause, mitigation steps, and action items.
Support Sarah: leaving thread open for final notes. thanks everyone. :heart:
